title: A Versatile Automated Platform for Micro-scale Cell Stimulation Experiments
protocol: Draw a sterile fibronectin solution into each microcapillary using the syringe pump.
Incubate the coated microcapillaries at 37°C for 2 hours.
Withdraw the fibronectin solution from the microcapillaries using the syringe pump.
Allow the microcapillaries to dry at room temperature for 6 hours.
Connect each fibronectin-coated microcapillary to polycarbonate tubing and then to a multi-port syringe pump.
Secure the body of each perfusion chamber to a heat block set to 37°C using tape.
Immerse the open ends of the perfusion chambers in a reservoir containing P388D.1 murine macrophages suspended in fresh growth medium at a concentration of 10^6 cells/ml.
Instruct the syringe pump to draw 10 μl of cell suspension (containing 10^4 cells) into each perfusion chamber followed by enough air to move the liquid plug.
Allow the cells to adhere to the fibronectin-coated interior surfaces of the perfusion chambers at 37 °C for 1 - 2 hr.
Transfer the open ends of the perfusion chambers from the cells reservoir to a new reservoir containing fresh growth medium.
Instruct the syringe pump to send the liquid plugs (conditioned media and unattached cells) to waste.
Withdraw fresh medium (10 μl).
Follow with enough air to position the new liquid plugs (fresh medium) over the adhered cells.
Continue to carry out medium exchanges at regular intervals (every 2 hr) until cell populations are sufficiently equilibrated and expanded.
Pattern the bottom plate of the DMF device with forty-six indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes by photolithography and etching.
Coat the patterned ITO electrodes with 5 μm of Parylene-C and 50 nm of Teflon-AF.
Form the top plate of the DMF device by coating an unpatterned ITO glass substrate with Teflon-AF.
Fix the DMF plates into a polymer cast with recesses that maintain a 400 μm spacing between the plates.
Insert Teflon-coated transfer microcapillaries into the space between the DMF plates, positioning each to extend to the edge of its cognate actuation electrode.
Affix a CapTite fitting to the opposite end of each transfer microcapillary.
Engage the electrical connectors to supply voltage to the ITO electrodes.
Automate electrode activation sequences through use of a computer-controlled electronic interface running pre-determined scripts.
Remove the open ends of the perfusion chambers from the medium reservoir.
Insert the open ends into CapTite fittings affixed to transfer microcapillaries of the DMF hub.
Instruct the syringe pump to send liquid plugs in perfusion chambers to waste.
Instruct the DMF hub to draw stimulus (E. coli BioParticles at 100 μg/ml) from an on-board reservoir.
Deliver a droplet of appropriate size (10 μl) to each transfer microcapillary.
Draw the stimulus plugs into the transfer microcapillaries with the syringe pump.
Follow with enough air to position the plugs over cell populations in perfusion chambers.
Incubate cells with stimulus at 37 °C for 1 - 4 hr.
Exchange for fresh stimulus by repeating steps to draw and deliver new droplets.
Terminate stimulation of cells.
Recover cell lysates for analysis.
Exchange the liquid plugs in the perfusion chambers for wash buffer if post-stimulation period is required.
Incubate as needed (5 min).
Exchange the liquid plugs (wash buffer) for lysis solution and incubate as needed (5 min).
Instruct the syringe pump to send the liquid plugs (cell lysates) to the DMF hub.
Disassemble the DMF hub carefully, remove the top plate of the DMF device using nitrogen gas without tilting sideways.
Collect the lysates using a Pipetman or syringe for off-platform analysis.
Immerse the transfer microcapillaries and CapTite fittings in 10% bleach (v/v in water) for 10 min at RT, rinse well with deionized water, dry using nitrogen gas.
Immerse the DMF device plates in 10% bleach for 10 min at RT, rinse well with isopropanol followed by deionized water, dry using nitrogen gas and bake at 160 °C for 10 min.
